rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Oxygen's chemistry splits along two axes. **Allotropy:** the same element appears as stable, colourless, paramagnetic, odourless **dioxygen O₂** (bond order 2, bp −183 °C) and as pale-blue, pungent, diamagnetic, unstable **ozone O₃** (bond order 1.5, bp −112 °C, forged from 3O₂ by +142 kJ of discharge energy and forever leaking its third oxygen as [O]).…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — One Element, Two Masks, Four Oxides Oxygen exists as two allotropes — the life-giving dioxygen O₂ and the pungent, reactive ozone O₃. And its compounds with other elements sort into **four oxide families** — acidic, basic, neutral, amphoteric (plus peroxides and mixed oxides) — a classification NEB loves because it tests both bonding and acid-base reasoning at once.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Allotropy and the two allotropes of oxygen - **Allotropy:** the existence of an element in two or more physical forms in the same physical state, differing in properties. Oxygen's allotropes: **dioxygen (O₂)** and **ozone (O₃, trioxygen)**. - O₂: colourless, odourless, paramagnetic (two unpaired electrons), bp −183 °C; the common, stable form.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: O2/O3 contrast: paramagnetic/diamagnetic, odourless/pungent, stable/unstable, bond order 2/1.5. Oxide sort: metal+water=alkali (basic); non-metal+water=acid; both acid and base=amphoteric; neither=neutral; O at -1=peroxide; Fe3O4 family=mixed. Period trend: Na2O basic, Al2O3 amphoteric, SO3 acidic.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Oxide classification follows behaviour, not element type: CO is a non-metal oxide yet neutral; ZnO is a metal oxide yet reacts with base — test with acid and alkali, then label.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Allotropy: same element, different forms, same state. O2: colourless, odourless, paramagnetic, bp -183 C, stable, bond order 2. O3: pale blue, pungent, diamagnetic, bp -112 C, unstable (3O2 = 2O3, dH = +142 kJ), bond order 1.5, strong oxidant (O3 -> O2 + [O]).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Earth's stratospheric ozone layer absorbs UV-B and UV-C; every 1 % thinning raises skin-cancer incidence measurably — allotropy with planetary stakes.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Why is CO neutral while CO2 is acidic?  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **CO is not acidic:** despite carbon being a non-metal, CO is a **neutral** oxide — it neither dissolves to an acid nor reacts with base. Classification follows behaviour, not element type.  ·  **Amphoteric ≠ neutral:** amphoteric oxides react with *both* acids and bases; neutral oxides react with *neither* — the distinction is tested every year.
